blazers.pulse: Still no game since Friday's 128-120 comeback win in Sacramento, so fans are riding a 2-0 start. The mood is glad for the W but uneasy about the defense, and some want the offense run through Deni Avdija more.
storylines: Portland came back from 12 down, powered by a 44-point third quarter, for its first road win
Rip City Project says the close call proves the Blazers must put the ball in Avdija's hands more after he took over in the second half
Defense worry: the Kings kept attacking Lillard and Morant, and Portland was slow closing out on corner threes
Shaedon Sharpe remains out with a torn right meniscus, expected back no earlier than February
Next up: at the Lakers on Tuesday night

timbers.pulse: Fans are still buzzing about Saturday's 3-2 win over Charlotte, won on Alexander Aravena's goal in the sixth minute of stoppage time. It snapped a seven-match winless run and pulled Portland within three points of the West's last playoff spot, so the season isn't dead yet.
storylines: Ariel Lassiter scored twice in the first half before Charlotte fought back to 2-2
The winner: Ian Smith's corner, flicked on by Cole Bassett, finished by Aravena at the goal line
Eric Izoita chipped in two assists
The win ended a 0-4-3 skid; Portland is 10-14-7 with 37 points, three back of the final West playoff spot
The loss kept Charlotte from clinching an East playoff berth

f1.pulse: Kimi Antonelli won Austin from pole, his ninth win of the year, but the title party has to wait at least a week. Russell finishing 8th and Hamilton 4th, each one spot better than Antonelli needed, kept it alive, so everyone's now looking at Mexico City.
storylines: Antonelli beat Leclerc by 13.078s, with Verstappen third
Antonelli leads Russell 365 to 242, a 123-point gap with 125 points left
Verstappen said Red Bull's pace and tyres weren't good enough and admitted the late Virtual Safety Car helped him hold off Hamilton
Ferrari bounced back on Sunday with Leclerc second after fading in qualifying
